title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 25-27). A is an abelian variety, or abelian scheme, in characteristic p. T_p(A)_et is the Tate module of the étale part of A[p^∞], a free Z_p-module of rank equal to the p-rank. The goal, completed on the next page, is a canonical isomorphism α_A: det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_et, built from a polarization φ and shown to be independent of φ.

Step 1: the polarization-dependent map. A polarization φ gives T_p(φ)_et: T_p(A)_et → T_p(A^∨)_et and hence a map of determinants. Normalized by the p-part of sqrt(deg φ), this gives α_p(φ).

Step 2: independence of φ (top of this page). Two polarizations differ by u = φ^{-1}φ', a Rosati-symmetric ('hermitien') totally positive element of End(A)⊗Q. Let Δ(u) be the p-adic determinant of u on the étale Tate module, transported via φ.
- The previous page gives deg u = det T_p(u)_et · det T_p(u*)_et.
- For symmetric u this yields Δ(u)^2 = deg u, so Δ(u) = ±sqrt(deg u), an integer.
- As u ranges over the lattice of symmetric endomorphisms (N = rank_Z of the hermitian part of End(A), not 'devra'), Δ is a polynomial in Q_p[T_1..T_N].
- It takes integer values on integer points, so its coefficients are rational (binomial-basis argument), and even p-integral.
- One must show Δ ≥ 0 on the positive cone, i.e. the sign ε(u) = +1 that the previous page worried about. It suffices to check this after extending scalars from Q to R. There End⊗R is a semisimple algebra with positive involution, so every positive hermitian u is w^2 with w hermitian and positive. Multiplicativity gives Δ(u) = Δ(w)^2 ≥ 0. Hence the normalization does not depend on φ.

Step 3: part b), that α_p(φ) really is an isomorphism and not merely an injection. This is equivalent to v_p(card Coker T_p(φ̃)_et) = v_p(sqrt(deg φ̃)). The next page proves it:
- Coker T_p(φ̃)_et ≅ (Ker φ̃)(p)_et.
- Ker φ̃ is self-dual, so its étale p-part is Cartier dual to its radicial part.
- Therefore (ord (Ker φ̃)(p)_et)^2 = ord Ker φ̃(p) = (deg φ̃)_p.

Result: a canonical, base-change compatible isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_et. As a consequence, det T_p(u)_et · det T_p(u*)_et = 1 for automorphisms u (next page).

The sign argument is the p-adic, étale-part analogue of the fact that deg φ_L = χ(L)^2 with χ(L) > 0 for ample L. Δ plays the role of a 'square root of the degree' polynomial on the Néron–Severi lattice.
errors: The claim that Δ is a polynomial on the hermitian lattice that is integer-valued at integer points is only sketched. It needs Δ(u) = ±sqrt(deg u) with deg u a perfect square for symmetric u, and polynomiality of u ↦ det T_p(u)_et with values in Z_p; neither is spelled out here.

Restricting to Δ on rational and real points requires Δ to have rational coefficients. That is derived from integrality of values, which is correct (a polynomial over a characteristic-0 field taking integer values on Z^N has rational coefficients) but rests on the previous point.
The struck-out passage contains the slip Z_p ∩ Q = Z_(p) versus Z_p[T] ∩ Q[T]. Grothendieck crossed it out himself.

ideas.what: Using a polarization to compare the étale parts of the p-divisible groups of A and A^∨, normalized by the p-part of sqrt(deg φ)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_et (p-rank of A equals p-rank of A^∨, at the determinant level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Equality of p-ranks is folklore (Mumford, Oort); I know no standard reference for the canonical determinant isomorphism

ideas.what: Sign/positivity of a 'square root of degree' polynomial on the positive cone, via the square-root argument in End⊗R with positive involution
ideas.modern_name: Positivity of the Rosati involution; deg φ_L = χ(L)^2 with χ(L) > 0 for ample L

ideas.what: A Q_p-polynomial that is integer-valued on Z^N has rational coefficients
v_p of the cokernel of T_p(φ)_et equals v_p(sqrt(deg φ)), via self-duality of Ker φ (étale part dual to radicial part)
ideas.modern_name: Cartier duality of the kernel of a polarization; étale/connected-local decomposition

missed.claim: A canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_et, independent of the polarization and compatible with base change, with the sign fixed by a positivity argument. Corollary: det T_p(u)_et · det T_p(u*)_et = 1 for automorphisms u. I am not aware of this determinant-level comparison being stated in the literature.
missed.quote: b) α_p(φ) induit bien un isom. de det T_p(A)_et avec det T_p(A^*)_et
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: On the ordinary or p-rank strata, det T_p(A)_et is the determinant of the Igusa-tower local system. A canonical identification with the dual side relates the Igusa structures of A and A^∨ (and the étale and multiplicative parts) without choosing a polarization. This is relevant to the p-adic modular forms / Hida theory bookkeeping of determinant characters. It is minor, though.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, essentially complete but small construction: a canonical determinant isomorphism with a neat sign argument. The ingredients are standard and the result is of modest importance, though apparently not stated as such in print.
transcription_corrections: 'N = rang_Z End(A)_{devra}' should almost certainly read 'End(A)_{herm}', the lattice of hermitian (Rosati-symmetric) endomorphisms.
'pour un prolongement[?] de Q à R' is likely 'pour le passage de Q à R', i.e. extension of scalars to R.
'un carré d'un élément hermitien[?] ≥ 0' reading is consistent with the argument, which takes square roots of positive hermitian elements.
'on sait de la sorte[?]' is probably 'on vient de le voir' or similar.
